Statement: High-frequency spectral anomalies (such as Fourier residual noise, DWT subbands, SRM residuals, and DCT statistics) serve as effective, interpretable indicators for detecting synthetic faces.

Statement: Popular benchmark deepfake and synthetic face datasets contain low-level statistical shortcuts and demographic/attribute imbalances (e.g., background noise, color/compression cues, facial attributes) that distort evaluation metrics.

Statement: Facial biometrics, physiological inconsistencies, and localized facial-region cues provide domain-grounded forensic evidence, though pure biometric margin erodes on high-realism generators.

Statement: Lossy JPEG compression, downscaling, and counter-forensic post-processing significantly degrade synthetic face detector accuracy and calibration by suppressing high-frequency forensic artifacts.
Contradicting Evidence: Space-frequency interactive convolutions (P0041), worst-of-K counter-forensic red-teaming with TTD (P0032), and language-guided contrastive training (P0034) substantially improve compression/perturbation resilience relative to vanilla CNNs, yet residual errors and calibration degradation persist under severe shifts (P0030 Table 3; P0033 Tables VII-VIII).

Statement: Uncalibrated binary synthetic-face detectors suffer severe overconfidence, threshold-shift collapse, and precision-recall cliffs under domain shift; explicit uncertainty calibration, OOD verification, and abstention reduce silent forensic errors.
Contradicting Evidence: Even calibrated ensembles (P0030) exhibit 6-10x ECE degradation under severe c40/blur shifts, and naive high confidence cutoffs (80%-85% in P0031) collapse recall to 18% unless paired with multi-dimensional confidence and structured abstention.
